input.summary:
Roofs part (parts/roofs.mjs): wing roof via roofWing now stops at the shell's gable frame, so the 5 refused writes at x=18..20, z=13, y=6..7 are dropped in the part rather than refused by runParts.
The main slate roof is applied by make.sh from roof.json, which is unchanged. OFF-PALETTE for this part was already empty.
make.sh now reports Roofs: 112 placed, refused 0, offPalette []; build.nbt is written with 1847 cells.
left: make.sh's main-roof run still prints a ROOF_BIG_PLANE warning (17-cell unbroken slope, no dormer or chimney) and 44 refused cells from the roof tool's keep/protect boxes. Both are outside the two reported problems, so I left them alone.
The wing roof's (18,7,13) and (20,7,13) stair cells are now dropped, so the shell's white_wool gable wall stands there. This is intended, but the wing gable should be rendered to confirm the look.

waste.what: Found which 5 cells collide only by running make.sh, then read roofWing and runParts source to see that the collisions came from the vocab helper rather than the part's own writes.
waste.cost: 2 make.sh runs and about 4 source reads to locate the 5 refusals
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for runParts (or mcd check against earlier parts) that lists a part's refused cells before the full build would have shown the 5 collisions and their owning helper in one step.

waste.what: Wrote a grid wrapper by hand (stopAtBuilt) to drop writes into cells the shell already built, because roofWing takes no protect/keep option and roof() only accepts one through its own call.
waste.cost: 1 Proxy written, 1 rerun; the fix is about 10 lines of glue
waste.tool: A runParts option (or build-library helper like addOnly(g)) that wraps the grid so helpers which write blindly silently skip earlier parts' cells, and roofWing forwarding a protect set to roof().
